sentences.text: Riabininohadros weberae is an extinct genus of ankylopollexian dinosaur, a group defined by specific ankle bone structures, that lived during the Maastrichtian stage.

The species was first described by Anatoly Nikolaevich Riabinin in 1945 based on hindlimb elements found in Crimea, though the fossils were actually discovered in 1934 near Bakhchysarai by Gertruda Weber.
While the discovery was reported in the scientific literature in 1937, a 2018 review revealed that the original describer had misidentified several fossil elements.

A juvenile skeleton excavated at Aleshino in 1965 was initially thought to belong to a different hadrosaurid species, but Roman Ulansky informally assigned it to Riabininohadros despite the genus being considered a nomen dubium until Lopatin and Averianov formally published it in 2020.

Lopatin and Averianov classified Riabininohadros as a primitive member of the Ankylopollexia, specifically the Styracosterna, based on its basal astragalus, placing it within the infraorder Iguanodontia.

Riabininohadros weberae lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 66 million years ago, in what is now Europe, with the fossil record spanning from 72.2 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian.
